2607.02403.title: ACID: Action Consistency via Inverse Dynamics for Planning with World Models
2607.02403.paper_summary: Decision-time planning with action-conditioned world models has become a popular paradigm for embodied control. However, the standard planning cost judges a candidate solely by how close its predicted terminal state lies to the goal, leaving the realizability of the intermediate transitions unchecked -- a predicted trajectory can look convincing while the environment rollout drifts away from it. In this paper, we propose ACID, a decision-time planning framework that introduces cycle action consistency: the action inferred backward from a predicted transition by an inverse dynamics model should recover the one that was conditioned on. We fold this per-step residual into the planning cost via a scale-invariant adaptive weight. Across four action-conditioned world models and six tasks spanning rigid and deformable manipulation, articulated control, and visual navigation, ACID consistently improves planning and matches the baseline's accuracy with substantially less planning compute.
2607.02403.paper_summary_zh: 決策時間規劃與行動條件世界模型已成為具身控制的一個流行範式。<lb/>然而，標準的規劃成本僅根據其預測的終端狀態與目標的接近程度來評判候選者，未檢查中間過渡的可實現性——預測的軌跡可能看起來令人信服，而環境的展開卻可能偏離它。<lb/>在本文中，我們提出了ACID，一個引入循環行動一致性的決策時間規劃框架：由逆動力學模型從預測過渡推斷出的行動應該恢復到被條件化的行動。我們通過一個尺度不變的自適應權重將這個每步的殘差折疊進規劃成本中。<lb/>在四個行動條件世界模型和六個涵蓋剛性和可變形操作、關節控制以及視覺導航的任務中，ACID始終改善規劃並以顯著較少的規劃計算匹配基準的準確性。
